That's the whole list settled — **20 behaviours**, all recorded as our baseline. Here's the complete picture of what we've shaped, in plain terms:

**Saving & editing**
- Paste a link; it gathers the title, description, icon and preview image; you correct before saving and can edit anytime. No duplicates. Non-links are declined.
- A separate **personal note** (with bold/italic/bullets/links) distinct from the page's description; edit the address, tags, note and title from one panel.

**Organising, finding & navigating** — the core
- Your own **tags** with fast reuse (type to narrow, or create new).
- **Search** across title, note, tags, site name and full address, with `#tag`, "phrases", and `AND`/`OR`/`NOT` grouping — plus a calm no-match state and graceful handling of a malformed search.
- Click a title/image to **open** the page; click a tag to **filter** the current view.
- **Sort** by date added, recently updated, or title.
- **Saved searches** (with included/excluded tags), remembered per view.

**Three spaces**
- **Collection**, **Reading list** (things you deliberately mark to read later), and **Archive** (put away, hidden from ordinary search, restorable). Search stays scoped to where you are.

**Working at scale**
- **Select many** (or all matching) and tag/untag, mark read/unread, archive/restore, or delete together.
- **Import** browser bookmarks (folders → tags, dates preserved, duplicates skipped) and **export** a portable file or full backup.
- **Preferences**: default sort, how many to show ("Show more"), and text size — remembered between visits.

**Trust & housekeeping**
- An **automatic in-app copy** of every saved page (the PDF for PDFs), plus a manual **Internet Archive** option.
- Quiet **saved/updated dates**, and permanent **Delete** (separate from Archive) always behind a clear confirmation.
- A calm layout that holds up with long text, many tags, and large lists.

I've also kept a short list of **non-functional wishes** for later (comfortable on the phone, snappy with hundreds of bookmarks, the "calm" feel, storage for page copies).

This fully covers your goal — *always being able to find and trust what you saved* — and everything in it you've operated and approved yourself.

**May I now switch from exploring to building this as the real application?** Just your go-ahead — or tell me anything that still feels unfinished.
